question.question: When designing a low-latency online prediction service for a high-throughput recommendation model, which architecture pattern best balances latency, scalability, and model freshness?

options.text: Batch inference with nightly model updates
Model deployed as a microservice with a feature store and online inference
Single monolithic service handling both training and inference
Serverless functions triggered per request with cold starts

question.explanation: Option B describes a decoupled microservice architecture that serves predictions in real time, leverages a feature store for up-to-date features, and can be scaled independently, providing low latency, high throughput, and fresh model versions. Batch inference (A) introduces high latency and stale predictions. A monolithic service (C) hampers scalability and makes independent updates difficult. Serverless functions (D) suffer from cold-start latency, which is unsuitable for strict low-latency requirements.
